I am that Odysseus, son of Laertes, who dwell in Ithaca, the island of rugged mountains, visible from afar; the island has two capes jutting out from it, and harbors with good anchorage. On it grows the olive tree, and a god has encircled it with the sea. But I, ranging far and wide, suffer grievous trials, as you now see.
